text: True or False: The Dutch book argument for probabilism is a synchronic coherence argument, showing that an agent whose credences violate the probability axioms is committed to accepting a set of bets that together guarantee a sure loss.
explanation: True. The synchronic Dutch book argument, due to Ramsey and de Finetti, shows that incoherent credences at a single time expose the agent to a combination of bets each deemed fair yet jointly guaranteeing a net loss, giving a pragmatic justification for probabilism. A separate diachronic Dutch book argument targets agents who plan to update by some rule other than conditionalization.
